data.one_liner: Intercept Android back-button taps with custom functions as an alternative to WillPopScope.
data.what_it_does: Allows developers to add custom interceptor functions that are executed when the device's back button is tapped. If any interceptor returns true, the default navigation pop action is prevented. Functions can be ordered using z-indexes and named for easy removal.
use_when: You need custom handling when the Android back button is pressed within stateful widgets.
You want an alternative to WillPopScope with support for multiple ordered interceptors.
avoid_when: You are using deep links with the GoRouter package, as it is currently incompatible.
You are relying strictly on standard declarative navigation routing without custom back handling.
strengths: Supports multiple ordered interceptors via z-index and registration order.
Allows both synchronous and asynchronous interceptor functions.
Provides test-friendly methods to simulate back button presses and inspect results.
weaknesses: Requires manual removal of interceptors in the dispose method to avoid memory leaks.
data.setup_notes: To make it work on Android 13 and up, set android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false" in the Android manifest.
